findings.source_passage: I don't see the idea of going to town... Plenty of gas... You can buy anything at a drugstore nowadays.
findings.source_locator: After the 'Her voice is full of money' passage, before Tom takes Gatsby's car — the drugstore line
findings.why_it_matters: Tom's 'You can buy anything at a drugstore nowadays' is the planted foreshadowing for the bootlegging reveal at the Plaza. Its removal weakens the structural irony of the later drugstore accusation.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Tom's 'Plenty of gas... you can buy anything at a drugstore nowadays' and the 'indefinable expression... passed over Gatsby's face' beat.

findings.source_passage: Wilson was so sick that he looked guilty, unforgivably guilty—as if he had just got some poor girl with child.
findings.source_locator: End of the garage scene, after 'difference between the sick and the well'
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of Nick's signature cruel-ironic similes and part of the critically engaged meditation on sickness; cutting it truncates the passage mid-thought.
findings.suggested_fix: Append the 'unforgivably guilty—as if he had just got some poor girl with child' clause to preserve the simile's sting.

findings.source_passage: The prolonged and tumultuous argument that ended by herding us into that room eludes me, though I have a sharp physical memory that, in the course of it, my underwear kept climbing like a damp snake around my legs
findings.source_locator: Just after arrival at the Plaza
findings.why_it_matters: The 'damp snake' underwear simile is vintage Nick voice — physical, comic, precise — and the 'crazy idea / five bathrooms / mint julep' origin of the suite is voice-establishing. The draft jumps straight to 'engaging the parlour of a suite,' erasing the texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the 'damp snake around my legs' image and the 'crazy idea' mint-julep origin of the suite.

findings.source_passage: Myrtle Wilson's body... left breast was swinging loose like a flap, and there was no need to listen for the heart beneath.
findings.why_it_matters: The brutal physical detail of the death is part of the novel's moral violence; the draft keeps only the mouth detail, softening the killing.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider restoring the 'left breast... swinging loose like a flap' clause to preserve the horror.

findings.source_passage: Gatsby stood in the centre of the crimson carpet and gazed around with fascinated eyes. Daisy watched him and laughed, her sweet, exciting laugh; a tiny gust of powder rose from her bosom into the air.
findings.source_locator: Buchanan salon, before the telephone-voice dialogue
findings.why_it_matters: The 'tiny gust of powder rose from her bosom' is a signature sensory image of Daisy's atmosphere; its loss thins the luncheon scene.

summary: Major Plaza-arc signatures, the 'voice of money / golden girl' coda, Pammy, 'Mr. Nobody from Nowhere,' 'So we drove on toward death,' and the pantry-window tableau are preserved; losses are medium-to-low voice trimmings (drugstore foreshadow, 'damp snake,' 'unforgivably guilty' simile, Daisy's powder, Myrtle's torn breast).
